# Enum types work across packages, and with bolero vet and bolero test.

bolero vet . ./colors
bolero test ./colors
stdout '^ok'

bolero run .
stdout '^red green blue$'
stdout '^true$'
stdout '^Red Blue$'
stdout '^runtime error: 5 is not a value of enum colors.Color$'

# Conversions and switches are checked for imported enum types too.
! bolero build ./bad
stderr 'switch on colors.Color has no case for Blue and no default case'
stderr 'cannot convert 7 \(untyped int constant\) to enum type colors.Color: 7 is not a value of colors.Color'
stderr 'operator \+ not defined on c .*: enum types only support comparison'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.26
-- colors/colors.bo --
package colors

type Color enum {
	Red
	Green
	Blue
}

func (c Color) Name() string {
	switch c {
	case Color::Red:
		return "red"
	case Color::Green:
		return "green"
	default:
		return "blue"
	}
}

// FromInt is inlined into callers in other packages, and the conversion
// must still be checked there.
func FromInt(n int) Color { return Color(n) }
-- colors/colors_test.bo --
package colors

import "testing"

func TestName(t *testing.T) {
	if got := Color::Green.Name(); got != "green" {
		t.Errorf("Color::Green.Name() = %q, want green", got)
	}
}

func TestString(t *testing.T) {
	if got := Color::Green.String(); got != "Green" {
		t.Errorf("Color::Green.String() = %q, want Green", got)
	}
}
-- main.bo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"example.com/m/colors"
)

func main() {
	var names []string
	for c := range colors.Color {
		names = append(names, c.Name())
	}
	fmt.Println(strings.Join(names, " "))
	fmt.Println(colors.FromInt(2) == colors.Color::Blue)

	// Enum types get a String method returning the value names.
	var s fmt.Stringer = colors.Color::Blue
	fmt.Println(colors.Color::Red, s.String())

	defer func() { fmt.Println(recover()) }()
	colors.FromInt(5)
}
-- bad/bad.bo --
package bad

import "example.com/m/colors"

func F(c colors.Color) {
	switch c {
	case colors.Color::Red, colors.Color::Green:
	}
	_ = colors.Color(7)
	_ = c + colors.Color::Red
}
